summary: Accepting an ISO-on-TCP connection is a fingerprint before any S7 message is exchanged, and a device that goes no further still belongs in the inventory.

device.description: Conpot running its default template, confirming a COTP connection at rack 0 slot 2
device.derivation: COTP_ConnectionConfirm.assemble in cotp.py packs the two references, an option field and the two TSAP parameters. s7_server.py calls it with the references of the request swapped and both TSAPs echoed. The confirm carries no TPDU size parameter even though the request does, which is a quirk of that implementation rather than of RFC 1006. The request here is the one this build sends to rack 0 slot 2, the default for the S7-300 and S7-400.

notes: device accepted an ISO-on-TCP connection, which indicates an S7 family controller
